rows: Define your claim first. Then tell me what would prove it.
Brawling is a noun. I want to know what it is doing.
A risk is a claim about probability. State yours.
Slow is a term. Define it before you use it on me.
The people deserve precision, not spectacle. Give them the exact thing.
The short of it: the claim is simple, and I can test it.
I am among the best only if the definition of best survives the test.
Take a look at the stance. It is a description, and I will check it.
Talk of technique. Describe the hold, not the applause. What actually worked?
The word strikes covers different things. Which kind do you mean?
A risk is only a claim until you measure what it costs.
Stalling is a word people use when they cannot define their plan.
The people want the truth about the contest. Give them a precise account.
You call yourself among the best. Define the term, then show me it applies.
You are proud of your {strength}. Define it for me. What exactly does it do?
I have tested your {strength}, and the result is narrower than you claim.
Composed, I see. Well done. A calm claim is easier to examine.
Noted. That is a precise point, and I accept it.
I could insult you about that. I would rather define the problem.
A single fall. Define the finish. Then keep me down if you can.
On the mat I will test every claim you make, one at a time.
Grounded or standing, the definition still applies.
Keep facing me. Show me what you mean by control.
That answer will do. It is precise, which is rare.
Still no answer from you. Define your answer, then give it.
Noted. I will note that as an accepted term.
Understood. We will test it at the bell.
I will test this match honestly and finish it on its terms.
My approach is exact. I say what I will do, and I do it.
Whatever happens, the result will match what was claimed.
The result is not defined yet. We will see what it turns out to be.
I have one more definition to offer, and you will see it when the bell rings.
